subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Show that the line 3x − 4y − 25 = 0 touches the circle x² + y² = 25.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.97 — Star Questions Plus, answer 204, printed under the banner "CIRCLES-VSAQ". The banner names the chapter and the mark cut, but a bank question's section is still OURS: it is classed VSAQ because it is a one-condition check with no derivation, which is the VSAQ shape; the SAQ chapter’s touching question, answer 48, also asks for the point of contact and is therefore longer. No appearance tag is printed beside it. The mark split 1 + 1 is OURS, not the book’s: the whole VSAQ chapter is set in two columns and prints no margin tags anywhere. There is no printed 2-mark split in this book to pattern it on, so it splits the answer at its one natural break. Star rank: the book’s VSAQ chapter table (book p.76) and its VSAQ hit list header (book p.11) both give the CIRCLE VSAQ chapter ★★★, but the chapter header printed on book p.77 shows only ★★. The two disagree; the TABLE’s rank is used, so every Circle VSAQ entry takes stars 3. That rank belongs to the CHAPTER, not to this question. Paper position: Maths-2B Section A runs Q1-Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory; Circle holds Q1 and Q2. Every number was re-derived and the book is correct: n² = 625 and r²(l² + m²) = 625. The book writes the right side as 25(3² + (−4²)), which is loose notation for 25(3² + (−4)²); the value 25 inside the bracket is right either way. Neither a two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Maths-2B: there is no TSBIE second-year Basic Learning Material on hand, and answer-book/papers/ holds first-year physics only. The book’s five Guess Papers (book pp.118-127) are the only stand-in, and the orchestrator diffs the authored set against them. insider_note: The tangential condition n² = r²(l² + m²) avoids the distance formula and its square root entirely, which is why it is the right tool for a 2-mark question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the tangential condition
steps.margin_note: One mark. Read l, m, n straight from the line as written, signs included.
steps.memory_tip: lx + my + n = 0 touches x² + y² = r² when n² = r²(l² + m²).
lines: The line touches the circle when
steps.why: The condition is the distance formula squared: |n|/√(l² + m²) = r becomes n² = r²(l² + m²). Squaring removes both the modulus and the root, so no surd appears anywhere.
common_mistakes: Taking n = 25 instead of −25, which happens to give the same square here but fails elsewhere.

steps.label: Check both sides
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Compute each side separately and then state the conclusion in words.

lines.text: ∴ The given line touches the given circle.

steps.why: Both sides come to 625, so the condition holds and the line is a tangent. If the left side were larger the line would miss the circle; if smaller, it would cut it at two points.
common_mistakes: Showing the two sides are equal but not writing the conclusion.
